ⓘ

These tools help with specific privacy tasks. net HUSH is not a VPN or proxy, and using this site doesn’t make your browsing anonymous. Know the differences.

TOOL 01 / SHARING

A link, with less baggage.

Remove common advertising and campaign parameters before you pass a link along.

Link cleaner

Fragments can point to a section, run an app, or hold important data. Keep them unless you know they’re unnecessary.

Careful by default

Removes utm_*, fbclid, gclid and other known click IDs. Keeps ordinary parameters such as searches, product IDs and referral fields that may be needed. Signed links are left alone.

A clean link can still lead to an unsafe page. This tool doesn’t scan destinations, unwrap redirects, remove every possible tracker, or hide your IP address. Preview and test the result before sharing.

TOOL 02 / ACCOUNTS

Something nobody would guess.

A fresh password, generated with your browser’s cryptographic random-number generator. No password is sent to net HUSH.

Password generator

Include characters

Generated only when you ask. Never saved by this site.

Give every account its own password.

Save it in a password manager you trust. Enable multi-factor authentication or use a passkey where supported. A long password helps, but it can’t protect you from handing it to a fake sign-in page.

Copying places the password on your system clipboard, which other software or clipboard sync may access. This page cannot reliably erase your clipboard. Closing the tab or clicking Clear removes the displayed password.

TOOL 03 / PHOTOS

Share the moment. Not the metadata.

Create a fresh PNG from your photo’s pixels, without carrying over the original embedded metadata.

Photo scrubber LOCAL PROCESSING

The file stays on your device. Nothing is uploaded.

Download clean PNG ↓

Visible faces, addresses, reflections and landmarks stay in the picture. Review the image before sharing. Colour and file size may change; animated images become a single frame. This is a new copy, not a change to your original.

What gets removed?

The browser decodes the image and redraws its pixels. The exported PNG keeps only the chunks needed to display those pixels, so the source EXIF (including GPS), IPTC, XMP, comments and original filename are not copied into the output. The generic filename is nethush-clean.png. Your operating system will still create filesystem timestamps for the downloaded copy.

TOOL 04 / AWARENESS

Your browser has a few things to say.

See some ordinary details available to a page. We display them here, without sending them anywhere.

Runs only when you click. No camera, location, microphone or network probes.

A glimpse, not a privacy score.

Language, screen size, timezone and other details can help sites tell visitors apart when combined. Browsers may reduce or disguise these values. This check does not determine whether you are unique, test your VPN, reveal your public IP, or check DNS and WebRTC leaks.

The server that delivers any website normally sees a connection IP address and request headers. A browser-only page cannot make that connection invisible.

FIELD NOTES / PLAIN ENGLISH

Privacy without the fog.

Different tools solve different problems. Start with the one you actually have.

Private browsing, a VPN, and Tor: what’s the difference?

Private browsing mainly limits what your browser saves locally after the session. It does not hide your IP address from websites or make you anonymous to your network.

A VPN routes traffic through a provider. Websites generally see the VPN’s exit IP, but you are shifting some trust to the VPN operator. Signed-in accounts, cookies and browser fingerprints can still identify you.

Tor Browser routes browsing through the Tor network and includes protections against fingerprinting. Logging into an identifying account still tells that service who you are. No tool guarantees anonymity.

Read the originals: Mozilla on private browsing → · Tor’s safe-use guidance →

Start with a small security plan.

Ask yourself: what information matters to me, who might want it, and what would happen if it leaked? A lost laptop, an advertising company, and a compromised email account call for different precautions.

Pick a realistic action: encrypt the laptop, limit sharing, or secure the email account and its recovery options. Revisit your plan when your circumstances change.

EFF: Your Security Plan →

Why clean a link or scrub a photo?

Links often contain campaign labels and click identifiers. Removing known ones can reduce what you pass along, but it doesn’t stop tracking at the destination.

Photos can carry metadata such as camera information, capture times and GPS coordinates. A fresh export can remove those records. What is visible in the picture can be just as revealing.

A quiet homelab is a maintained homelab.

Keep private dashboards off the public internet unless there is a clear reason to expose them. Review which ports are forwarded, keep software updated, use strong authentication, and test your backups.

DNS filtering can block requests to known domains; it cannot block every tracker or make your browsing anonymous. Self-hosting gives you control and the responsibility to maintain it.

Is net HUSH still an anonymous web proxy?

No. The original site offered anonymous surfing through a proxy. This version is a set of local tools and plain-language guides. It does not relay websites, change your IP address or tunnel traffic. If anonymous browsing is your goal, read the Tor Project’s guidance and understand its limits.

THEN & NOW

An old address. A familiar idea.

Before the feeds, the pop-ups asking to track you, and the internet in your pocket, there was net HUSH.

net HUSH

free anonymous surfing

THE ORIGINAL SPIRIT, CIRCA 2001

Back then: a quieter way to surf.

The original net HUSH was built around anonymous surfing. Its blue bars, small sidebar and direct approach belonged to an internet of personal sites, useful little services and links worth keeping.

Today: a few useful ways to share less.

The privacy problems have changed. Links carry identifiers. Pictures can carry locations. Browsers reveal details. Every new account wants one more piece of you.

This reboot keeps the simplicity and independence. Small tools that run in your browser. Clear explanations of what they can and cannot do. Source you can read and host yourself.

You shouldn’t need to hand over more information to take a little less of it online.

What might come next?

A downloadable offline toolkit, more practical homelab privacy guides, and a carefully designed self-hosted sharing service are possible directions. They’re ideas for the future, not features running here today.

Explore the project on GitHub →

NO FINE-PRINT MAZE

Less collected. Less to worry about.

Here is what this version of net HUSH actually does.

Your tool inputs stay here.

The link cleaner, password generator, photo scrubber and browser check run in this tab. This application does not upload their inputs or results. It includes no analytics, advertising scripts, external fonts or tracking pixels, and makes no background API calls.

No account. No cookies from this application.

The checklist stays in memory unless you enable “Remember my checklist”. That setting stores only your checkmarks in this browser’s local storage. Turn it off, or use Reset checklist, to remove the saved checklist.

Loading a website still makes a connection.

Your hosting provider, CDN or reverse proxy may receive and log connection information such as IP addresses, request headers and timestamps. Their policies and configuration govern those records. A hosted preview may also use platform authentication. This page is not a promise that the hosting infrastructure keeps no logs.

You choose what leaves the page.

Copy buttons use your clipboard only when clicked. Downloads create a file on your device. External links connect to other websites when you follow them, with this page’s referrer suppressed. We cannot control how your browser extensions, operating system or those sites handle data.

Useful tools, with clear limits.

net HUSH is not a proxy, VPN, malware scanner or audited security product. It cannot promise anonymity, check every form of tracking, or protect a compromised device. Use the source to inspect what it does.
